what: a stout fighting dagger: a short, very broad, straight double-edged blade shaped like a long triangle, only as long as the grip and pommel together, a small straight crossguard, a short thick grip and a round pommel.
colours: The blade, guard and pommel are pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The grip is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the pommel at the bottom left corner and the point at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: broad triangular blade no longer than the hilt

what: a short sword of the Roman kind: a broad, flat, straight double-edged blade about three times as long as its grip, its edges parallel and coming to a short triangular point, a small thick oval guard no wider than the blade, a short grip and a big round ball pommel.
colours: The blade, guard and pommel are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The grip is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the ball pommel at the bottom left corner and the point at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: blade very wide for its length
small guard no wider than the blade

what: a one-handed knightly arming sword: a straight double-edged blade of middling width, four times as long as its grip, tapering evenly to a sharp point, a straight bar crossguard clearly wider than the blade, a short one-hand grip and a flat disc pommel.
colours: The blade, crossguard and pommel are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The grip is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the pommel at the bottom left corner and the point at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: straight crossguard wider than the blade

what: a knight's longsword: a long straight double-edged blade with a central groove, a plain straight crossguard, a two-hand grip and a wheel pommel.

pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the pommel at the bottom left corner and the point at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: long straight blade with a groove

what: a hand-and-a-half war sword: a long, heavy, very broad straight double-edged blade with a raised central ridge, a thick crossguard whose two arms slant forward towards the blade like a shallow letter V, a long grip with room for a hand and a half, bound in the middle by one steel ring, and a pear-shaped pommel.
colours: The blade, crossguard, grip ring and pommel are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The grip is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the pommel at the bottom left corner and the point at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: crossguard arms slanting towards the blade
long grip with a steel ring in the middle

what: a two-handed greatsword: an enormous straight double-edged blade, extremely broad from the guard almost to the tip, with a wide central groove, a long thick straight crossguard with blunt square ends, a very long two-handed grip a quarter of the whole sword's length, and a heavy faceted pommel.
colours: The blade, crossguard and pommel are pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The long grip is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the pommel at the bottom left corner and the point at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.

what: a zweihander, a giant two-handed sword: a very long, broad, straight double-edged blade and a very long two-handed grip with a pear pommel. Two steel bars cross it: the main crossguard, very wide, at the top of the grip; and, a hand's width further up the blade, a second crossbar half as wide with pointed ends. Between the two bars the blade is plain and blunt.
colours: The blade, both crossbars and the pommel are pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The long grip is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the pommel at the bottom left corner and the point at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: two crossbars: a wide crossguard and a smaller one further up the blade

what: a rapier: a long, straight, slender thrusting blade, drawn thicker than life so that it is as thick as a finger, ending in a needle point, with a big rounded steel cup guard like a half ball covering the hand, one curved knuckle bar sweeping from the cup to the pommel, a short grip and a small round pommel.
colours: The blade, cup guard, knuckle bar and pommel are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The grip is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the pommel at the bottom left corner and the point at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.

what: a scimitar: a broad single-edged blade that curves strongly backward in one deep arc like a crescent, growing wider towards the tip and ending in a clipped point, a small crossguard with two short knobs, and a grip whose pommel hooks forward.
colours: The blade, crossguard and pommel cap are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The grip is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a diagonal, the hooked pommel at the bottom left corner and the tip at the top right corner, the curved back of the blade bulging towards the lower right, the whole thing inside the picture.

what: a hatchet, a small hand axe: a short stout wooden haft with one wedge-shaped steel axe blade at its top end. The blade sticks out on one side of the haft only and flares to a gently curved cutting edge; the other side of the haft is bare wood. The haft is only three times as long as the blade is tall.
colours: The axe blade is pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The haft is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with a dark brown leather wrap at the bottom.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the haft at the bottom left corner and the axe blade at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: one blade on one side only

what: a battleaxe: a long straight wooden haft with one big bearded axe blade at its top end. The blade sticks out on one side of the haft only, flaring to a long curved cutting edge whose lower corner hangs down in a beard; on the opposite side there is only a short blunt steel hammer-knob. The haft is four times as long as the blade is tall, with two steel bands below the head.
colours: The axe blade, the knob and the two bands are pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The haft is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with a dark brown leather wrap at the bottom.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the haft at the bottom left corner and the axe blade at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: one big bearded blade on one side only

what: an executioner's great axe for two hands: a very long thick wooden haft with one enormous axe blade at its top end. The blade sticks out on one side of the haft only and is a huge half-moon, its curved edge as long as a third of the haft; on the opposite side one short thick steel spike points backward; a steel spear-spike caps the top of the haft.
colours: The half-moon blade, the back spike and the top spike are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The haft is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with a dark brown leather wrap at the bottom.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the haft at the bottom left corner and the huge blade at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: one huge half-moon blade on one side

what: a double-headed great axe for two hands: a very long thick wooden haft with two enormous matching axe blades at its top end, one on each side of the haft, back to back and mirror images of each other, each a broad crescent with its curved edge facing outward.
colours: Both axe blades and the socket between them are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The haft is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with a dark brown leather wrap at the bottom.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the haft at the bottom left corner and the double axe head at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: two matching blades, one each side

what: a heavy war club carved from one thick tree limb: it is thick everywhere, as thick as a forearm at the grip and widening gradually and evenly to twice that at its blunt rounded far end, a long cone with a rounded top. Its surface is rough with three or four big knots. It is one single piece with no separate head.
colours: The whole club, from the grip to the thick end, is pure colourless neutral grey, light grey on the ridges and charcoal grey in the grain, exactly as wood looks in a black-and-white photograph. Only the grip at the narrow end is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the narrow grip at the bottom left corner and the thick end at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: grey all over except the grip

what: a knight's mace made all of metal: a short thick steel rod for a handle and, at its top, a heavy head that is a round ball ringed with six thick blunt vertical ribs running from top to bottom, with deep dark grooves between them, capped by a small knob.
colours: The ribbed head and the rod are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The lower half of the handle is wrapped in dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the grip at the bottom left corner and the ribbed head at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.

what: a morningstar: a short thick wooden handle and, fixed solidly on its top end, a big round iron ball bristling with a dozen thick sharp cone-shaped spikes pointing out in every direction, each spike as long as a thumb. The ball sits directly on the handle.
colours: The spiked ball and the collar under it are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The handle is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the handle at the bottom left corner and the spiked ball at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: ball fixed directly on the handle

what: a military flail: a short thick wooden handle; from an iron cap on its top end hangs a short chain of four very big thick oval iron links; and on the end of the chain a round iron ball studded with short thick spikes. Handle, chain and ball are all joined in one line and touch each other.
colours: The cap, the chain and the spiked ball are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The handle is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age.
pose: It lies stretched out straight on a diagonal: the butt of the handle at the bottom left corner, then the chain pulled taut in the same line, and the spiked ball at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: all three joined in one piece
grey ball and chain, brown handle
must_not_show: ball fixed directly on the handle

what: a one-handed war hammer of the plain kind: a short stout wooden handle with a blocky hammer head set crosswise on its top end like the bar of a letter T. Both ends of the head are flat square striking faces; the head is as long as a third of the handle.
colours: The whole hammer head is plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The handle is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with a dark brown leather wrap at the bottom.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the handle at the bottom left corner and the hammer head at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: blocky head with two flat faces

what: a knight's warhammer: a long straight wooden haft with a steel head set crosswise on its top end. One end of the head is a square toothed hammer face; the opposite end is one long thick curved spike coming to a point; a short spike sticks up from the top of the haft; two steel strips run down the haft from the head.
colours: The hammer face, the curved spike, the top spike and the strips are pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The haft is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with a dark brown leather wrap at the bottom.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the haft at the bottom left corner and the head at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: long curved beak on the other side

what: a two-handed maul: a very long, very thick wooden haft with a gigantic head set crosswise on its top end like the bar of a letter T: a massive rectangular block of iron, with two broad flat square striking faces and thick raised bands round each end. The head is as long as a third of the haft and twice as thick as the haft.
colours: The whole gigantic head is plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The haft is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with a dark brown leather wrap at the bottom.

must_show: enormous block head with two flat faces

what: a fighting quarterstaff: one perfectly straight, thick, plain round wooden pole, the same thickness from end to end, as thick as a wrist. Both ends are simply sawn off flat. A band of leather wrapping covers the middle third of the pole.
colours: The whole pole, end to end, is pure colourless neutral grey, light grey on the ridges and charcoal grey in the grain, exactly as wood looks in a black-and-white photograph. The wrapping round the middle is dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, one blunt end at the bottom left corner and the other blunt end at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: brown leather wrap in the middle

what: a wanderer's walking staff cut from a tree limb: a tall, thick, slightly crooked pole with a few knots and bumps along it, thicker towards the top, where it ends in a big gnarled twisted knot of root. The bottom end is a blunt point.
colours: The whole staff, the pole and the gnarled knot alike, is pure colourless neutral grey, light grey on the ridges and charcoal grey in the grain, exactly as wood looks in a black-and-white photograph. One short band of wrapping below the knot is dark brown leather.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the blunt bottom end at the bottom left corner and the gnarled knot at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: big twisted knot at the top

what: a war spear: a very long straight thick wooden shaft with one broad leaf-shaped steel spearhead on its top end, the spearhead as wide as three shaft-widths, with a central rib and a short socket; a small pointed steel cap on the bottom end.
colours: The spearhead, its socket and the small bottom cap are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The shaft is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the shaft at the bottom left corner and the spearhead at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: broad leaf-shaped spearhead at the top only

what: a glaive: a very long straight wooden pole with one broad single-edged curved blade fixed to its top end, its cutting edge bulging to one side and its tip curving back to a point.
colours: The blade and its socket are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The pole is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with two iron-grey bands.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the butt of the pole at the bottom left corner and the blade at the top right corner. The pole is four times as long as the blade. The whole thing is inside the picture.

what: a halberd: a very long straight wooden pole whose top end carries three steel parts in one head: a broad axe blade sticking out on one side, a curved hook pointing out on the opposite side, and a long straight spear spike pointing forward off the end of the pole.
colours: The axe blade, the hook and the spear spike are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The pole is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age, with steel strips below the head.

what: a short hunting bow, drawn very thick and chunky: one single curved stave of wood and one string, nothing else. The bow is only eight times as long as its stave is thick: the stave is a fat round bar, as thick as a strong man's forearm at the grip in its middle and still as thick as a thumb at the two tips, each tip simply rounded off. The stave bends in one plain even curve, the same curve from end to end, like a crescent moon, with no kink and no backward bend at the tips. From one tip to the other runs one straight taut string, a rope as thick as a finger. The gap between the grip and the string is a quarter of the bow's length. It has no arrow.
colours: The whole stave is pure colourless neutral grey, light grey in the highlights and charcoal in the shadows, exactly as it would look in a black-and-white photograph. The grip in the middle is wrapped in dark brown leather. The string is off-white.
pose: It stands leaning: its lower tip at the bottom left corner and its upper tip at the top right corner, the curve of the stave bulging towards the upper left and the straight string on the lower right side, the whole bow inside the picture.
must_show: one very thick, evenly curved stave
thick straight string from tip to tip

what: a horseman's recurved composite bow: a thick stave with a double curve: each limb curves away from the grip and then its tip sweeps back the other way in a strong hook, with a set-back grip in the middle, strung tip to tip with one taut thick cord. It has no arrow.
colours: Both limbs of the stave are plain neutral mid-grey with pale grey highlights and dark grey grain and no tint of colour in it. The grip in the middle and a binding below each hooked tip are dark brown leather. The cord is off-white.
pose: It stands leaning: its lower tip at the bottom left corner and its upper tip at the top right corner, the curve of the stave bulging towards the upper left and the straight string on the lower right side, the whole bow inside the picture.

what: a war longbow as tall as a man: one very tall, thick, gently curved stave, as thick as a wrist at the middle grip and tapering to both tips, each tip capped with a small notched nock, strung tip to tip with one taut thick cord. It has no arrow.

pose: It stands leaning: its lower tip at the bottom left corner and its upper tip at the top right corner, the curve of the stave bulging towards the upper left and the straight string on the lower right side, the whole bow inside the picture.

what: a light hunting crossbow, small and simple, seen from directly above as it lies flat. It is made of two parts that together make the shape of a cross. Part one, the stock: one short straight thick beam of dark wood with a plain rounded butt, running straight from the bottom left to the top right, its butt at the bottom left. Part two, the bow: one short thick bow of steel, only two thirds as wide from tip to tip as the stock is long, one single curved bar exactly like a short archer's bow, fixed by its middle flat across the stock a little way back from the stock's top-right end, at a right angle to the stock, so that one arm of the bow sticks out towards the upper left and the other arm sticks out towards the lower right. Both arms are the same length, and both tips bend back a little towards the butt. One thick pale cord, the string, as thick as a finger, runs in one straight line from one tip of the bow to the other, crossing over the top of the stock. It has no stirrup and no crank: only the short stock, the short bow and the string.
colours: The bow is pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The stock is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age. The string is off-white.
pose: It lies flat, seen from directly above: the butt of the stock at the bottom left corner and the front of the stock at the top right corner; the bow crosses the stock near its front, one arm reaching towards the top left and the other towards the bottom right. The whole thing is inside the picture.
must_show: short wooden stock with one short steel bow across its front, an arm each side
a straight string from tip to tip
must_not_show: bow arm on one side only

what: a soldier's crossbow, sturdy and plain, seen from directly above as it lies flat. It is made of two parts that together make the shape of a cross. Both arms are the same length, and both tips bend back a little towards the butt. One thick pale cord, the string, as thick as a finger, runs in one straight line from one tip of the bow to the other, crossing over the top of the stock. It has no stirrup and no crank: only the long heavy stock, the broad bow and the string.
colours: The bow is pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The stock is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age. The string is off-white.
pose: It lies flat, seen from directly above: the butt of the stock at the bottom left corner and the front of the stock at the top right corner; the bow crosses the stock near its front, one arm reaching towards the top left and the other towards the bottom right. The whole thing is inside the picture.
must_show: long heavy wooden stock with one broad steel bow across its front, a long arm each side
a straight string from tip to tip
must_not_show: bow arm on one side only

what: a heavy siege crossbow, an arbalest: a long, very thick wooden stock bound with three broad steel bands, and across its front end one enormous, very thick steel bow, an arc with two long equal arms, one on each side of the stock, as wide from tip to tip as the stock is long. The crossbow is cocked: a thick pale cord runs from the tip of each bow arm back to a catch on top of the stock halfway along it, so the cord makes a wide letter V with its point on the stock, and the bow and the cord together make a triangle with the stock running through its middle. On the very front tip of the stock is an iron stirrup loop, and on the butt end a small steel winding crank with two handles.
colours: The enormous bow, the three bands, the stirrup and the crank are pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph. The stock is dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age. The cord is off-white.
pose: It lies flat, seen from above and a little from one side: the butt of the stock at the bottom left corner and the front of the stock at the top right corner. The bow crosses the front of the stock at a right angle, one arm reaching towards the top left and the other towards the bottom right, both arms the same length. The whole thing is inside the picture.
must_show: thick banded stock with a very wide, very thick bow across its front
cord drawn back in a V
stirrup at the front, crank at the butt
must_not_show: bow arm on one side only

what: a handful of three arrows bound together side by side with one turn of cord round the middle: each arrow has a thick straight wooden shaft, a broad barbed triangular arrowhead and three trimmed feathers at the tail. The three lie close and parallel, touching, heads together.
colours: The three arrowheads are plain neutral grey steel with bright white highlights and dark grey shadows and no tint of colour in it. The shafts are dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age. The feathers are dark russet-brown hawk feathers. The cord is dark brown.
pose: The bundle lies on a straight diagonal, the feathered tails at the bottom left corner and the three arrowheads at the top right corner, all inside the picture.
must_show: broad arrowheads together at the top right

what: a handful of three crossbow bolts lying side by side and touching, bound together with one turn of dark cord round the middle. Each bolt is short and fat: a stubby round wooden shaft as thick as a thumb and only six times as long as it is thick, the same thickness all along. At the top-right end each shaft is simply sharpened into a short plain steel point, a small smooth cone no wider than the shaft itself, like the tip of a sharpened pencil capped in steel. At the bottom-left end each shaft has two short stiff vanes of dark leather, small flat fins no longer than the shaft is thick. The three points lie together at one end and the three vaned tails together at the other.
colours: The three small points are pure colourless neutral grey, light grey in the highlights and charcoal in the shadows, exactly as it would look in a black-and-white photograph. The stubby shafts are dark walnut-brown wood, scuffed and darkened with age. The vanes are dark brown leather. The cord is dark brown.
pose: The bundle lies on a straight diagonal, the three vaned tails at the bottom left corner and the three small steel points at the top right corner, all inside the picture.
must_show: three short fat bolts in one bundle
small plain cone points no wider than the shafts
short stubby vanes at the bottom left

what: a shepherd's sling for throwing stones: one long braided leather cord, as thick as a thumb, laid out in a tall loop shaped like a teardrop. At the top of the loop the two ends of the cord cross each other once and stick out a little way, one ending in a small finger loop and the other in a knot. The inside of the loop is empty and the backdrop shows through it. There is no stone.
colours: The braided cord and the small cradle are pure colourless neutral grey leather, light grey on the ridges and charcoal grey in the creases, exactly as leather looks in a black-and-white photograph.
pose: It lies flat, seen from directly in front: the small cradle at the bottom, the loop of cord above it, and the two crossed ends at the top.
must_show: a loop of thick braided cord
small oval cradle at the bottom of the loop
two cord ends crossed at the top

what: a thief's lockpick: one single flat strip of steel, thick as a finger. At the handle end the strip widens into a small round finger ring. The far end narrows and its last small bit bends upward into one tiny tooth. It is drawn very thick and bold.
colours: The whole lockpick is pure colourless neutral grey steel, light grey in the highlights and charcoal grey in the shadows, exactly as steel looks in a black-and-white photograph.
pose: It lies on a straight diagonal, the handle end with its hole at the bottom left corner and the hooked tip at the top right corner, the whole thing inside the picture.
must_show: straight strip with one small bent tooth at the tip
